items.rationale: Overvoltage cover 2.3.3 applies to a damaged appliance, but nothing was surge-protected, so indemnity is halved. Reference speaker prices were about 250-520 gross, so I assume roughly 400 before the halving.
7.1.9 limits indemnity to a standard-grade equivalent of the 55-inch LED set. References put that at about 520-600, and the 50% unprotected reduction brings it to about 280.
Undamaged accessories are not established as affected under 7.1.5, and the references put this at near zero.
Not physically damaged, and mounting items are not repair costs. The references put this at near zero.
No damage is established, and 7.1.5 and 7.1.6 do not extend cover to undamaged items of a set.
The console was not affected by the surge, so 4.2.4 and 7.1.5 exclude it.
Delivery of replacement property is excluded under 7.1.8(b).
Fitting and commissioning of replacement property is excluded under 7.1.8(c).
The contractor's own diagnostics and documentation are excluded under 7.1.8(e) and the service-order exclusion in 3.1.5, so this is not a repair cost. References put it at about zero.

items.description: Wiring safety check of distribution board
items.rationale: The wiring was not damaged and the check is not a repair cost, so 7.1.5 and 7.1.8 exclude it.
Under 7.1.8(d) an attendance charge follows the work billed on the same invoice, and that invoice has no indemnifiable work.
